memories.content: The user stores prepared meals on the second shelf of the freezer.
The user went to the market without a shopping list and bought onions that were already at home.
On a day the user shopped after checking a refrigerator photo, they did not make a duplicate purchase.
On a day the user made a spicy stew, they left part of one bowl uneaten.
The next time the user cooked it, they used half as much chili powder and finished the meal.
When cooking with their younger brother, the user assigned the cooking sequence only verbally and they did the same task twice.
The next time, the user and their younger brother split ingredient preparation and heat control and finished the meal 20 minutes earlier.
When cooking together, the user's younger brother prefers to divide the cooking and dishwashing roles in advance.
The local agent can compare responses across several meals, but it cannot conclude from one unfinished food item that the user dislikes that ingredient.
The condition of frozen prepared food may vary with its packaging and storage duration.
The user keeps basic repair tools in a box beneath the sink.
On a day the faucet leaked, the user placed only a towel beneath it, and the floor became wet as well.
After sending a photo to building management, the user finalized the time for a repair visit.
Before the technician's visit, the user emptied the area beneath the sink so work could begin immediately.
On a day the user wrote the visit time only in the calendar and turned off the reminder, they heard the doorbell late.
For the next visit, the user enabled a reminder 30 minutes beforehand and answered immediately at the entrance.
After the repair, the user called their maternal aunt to confirm that the spare key entrusted to her was still there.
The user's maternal aunt considers it unsafe to hand the spare key to a repair technician without the user's explicit request.
Obtain the user's reconfirmation before scheduling an external worker to enter the residential unit.
A multi-unit residential building's repair schedule may change because of emergency work or parts availability.

analysis.overview: The frames contain independent household contexts: the reference covers food storage, shopping, cooking, and cautious preference inference, while the compared frame covers leak response, repair access, reminders, spare-key safety, and schedule uncertainty. No claim directly governs the same operational decision across frames.
